fundamentals.capability: An operation writes one record per member of a set that is computed at run time (a group expanded to its members, a recipient list, a thread's participants), with a per-recipient dedupe key and no fixed upper count known at declaration time.
fundamentals.why: tenant-operation-step (specifications/boundary.jsonc) is a fixed list of create-record, update-record, delete-record, post-ledger, reverse-ledger, find-record, branch and write-setting steps over the subject and one reference. There is no loop or fan-out step, and the showcase gap 8 records that operations have no conditional steps and no lookups. A message to N recipients, a notice to N recipients and a receipt per participant therefore cannot be written in one operation. docs/protocol.md and design-system.md show no per-row operation either (showcase gap 6: per-row actions refused).

fundamentals.capability: One ordered, paged read whose rows come from several record types or sources (for example held changes, held actions, orders and content in review as one inbox; or a timeline merged from domain events and records), with each source filtered by the viewer's rights.
fundamentals.why: query-def (boundary.jsonc) names one object type (object: object-type-id) and one filter; view-section names one query. No query unions object types. showcase README gap 1 (a product names only its own entities) and gap 8 (no query by field) bear on this. The approvals inbox merges four sources (contract 12.7) and home.summary composes several module reads (packages/engine/src/suite/handlers/home.ts calls sub-actions).

fundamentals.capability: Text search over one or several record types with ranking (prefix match above word-start match above substring match), a per-type limit, a total count per type, and text search over child rows (message bodies) reached from a parent (thread subject or body).
fundamentals.why: Strata has a platform search index (boundary.jsonc gateway-reads-search-index, runtime-writes-search-index), but query-def has a filter expression and no ranked text match; the expression grammar has contains (boundary.jsonc 'contains') without ranking. Search across twelve types with per-type totals (contract 12.10) and body search over messages (contract 12.2, to_tsvector) have no declaration.

fundamentals.capability: A human task as a platform primitive: assignee, status with transitions, priority, due date, comments, history, optimistic version and an inbox of a principal's tasks, with notification on assignment.
fundamentals.why: Strata has no task object. Tasks would be an ordinary product object, but the product cannot express the task inbox or the assignment notification and history without a primitive (WG-5496 names exactly this gap). Human-task steps in workflows exist only as approve-workflow-step and automation-approval (boundary.jsonc), which are approvals, not assignments.

fundamentals.capability: A write that commits only when the stored state still matches what the caller read (a version check, or a state precondition such as status is pending), and returns a named refusal (STALE_VERSION, INVALID_TRANSITION, approval already decided) when it does not, with concurrent attempts resolved by one winner.
fundamentals.why: An operation can carry conditions, but a condition failure is a generic refusal with no named reason and no returned current state (boundary.jsonc tenant-operation-step has no guard; showcase gap 8). Plinth needs STALE_VERSION with current_version and approval 'already decided' with the status, so the client can re-read. WG-5488 is the Strata task for concurrent approval decisions conditional on state.

fundamentals.capability: An operation that a policy holds for another principal's approval: the stored input is kept with a hash, the approver decides, and on approval the operation runs later as the original requester with the approver recorded as approved_by, with expiry and a result or failure record.
fundamentals.why: Strata's approval primitives are workflow steps (approve-workflow-step, automation-approval in boundary.jsonc) and proposals (propose-change, approve-proposal). A held operation that replays its stored input as the requester and records approved_by is not declared. Plinth keeps this in action_approvals with approver_permission per action (contract 3.8, 12.7). WG-5488 covers the decision side only.

fundamentals.capability: An agent or a service acting for a human, with the delegator recorded on every write and event (on_behalf_of), and separation of duties that refuses a decision by the requester or by the person the requester acted for.
fundamentals.why: Strata's agent path (propose-change, approve-proposal, agent-gateway in boundary.jsonc) records a delegator for agent calls, but a product policy cannot name the on_behalf_of person as a condition on the approver, and an operation cannot store a second principal per record. Plinth's SoD rule (contract 3.8: human, not requester, not on_behalf_of) needs both. WG-5499 covers delegation.

fundamentals.capability: A signed-in principal lists its own sessions (browser tabs and MCP connections), revokes one of them from a product screen, and every open socket of that session is closed and refused with a named reason, with the owner held as the session's principal.
fundamentals.why: Strata has platform sessions with list-sessions, revoke-session (step-up 15 min, requires session-manage) and revoke-other-sessions (boundary.jsonc CT-061, CT-1025), and notices carry session revocations. These are identity-service intents for the platform's own sessions, not product-declared, and the owner-only self-service path is not offered to product screens (showcase gap 2: role-restricted screens absent). Plinth's per-tab session header is not a Strata concept.

fundamentals.capability: Aggregate counts shown in the shell (unread, pending, open, attention) that are pushed to each principal's connection after any change that affects them, computed for that principal with one query, without the client re-reading.
fundamentals.why: Strata has live bindings and change notices (boundary.jsonc live-* bindings, notice-queue) that re-render a view when its data changes, but the view must be read again and there is no per-principal count frame. Plinth's counts frame (contract 6.1) recomputes NavCounts for the principal after a count-affecting event. The live binding set is fixed per screen; a count across records owned by several modules has no declaration.

fundamentals.capability: A write derives reference fields from free text at commit time (for example the @handle mentions in a body become references to the mentioned people), using a declared grammar, so that the mention set is stored with the text and cannot be spoofed by the client.
fundamentals.why: The tenant rule language cannot parse text (contract 1.7 says mentions are an inline grammar rendered client-side). Strata operations take values from inputs and the subject, not computed from a string field (tenant-operation-step; showcase gap 8). A client-supplied mention list could be forged and would not notify correctly.

fundamentals.capability: A page assembled from configurable widgets, each a self-contained block bound to its own data, with a personal copy of a system page per member, layout on a grid, and route parameters bound into widget config.
fundamentals.why: Strata screens are fixed view sections and forms (ui-form, ui-action, view-section in boundary.jsonc), and showcase gap 5 records that the interpreter draws fixed sections, not composed widgets, and has no frame slots. Plinth's pages are Page and Widget nodes laid out on a 12-column grid (contract 5A.1). WG-5464 covers compositions.

fundamentals.capability: Composite interaction patterns as registry entries: master and detail in one screen (list selects, detail follows), a thread view with replies and receipts, a kanban board with keyboard moves, and a decision form with a reason field and a diff, each reusable by any product.
fundamentals.why: The design system (docs/design-system.md layers 2 and 3) defines primitives and patterns, and gestures (<ds-sortable>, <ds-lanes>) with keyboard paths, but no master-detail or thread or decision composite is in the pattern catalogue. Plinth's widgets implement these in packages/web/src/widgets. WG-5479 covers composite patterns and the renderer registry.

fundamentals.capability: Pointer gestures on collections (move a card between lanes, reorder, multi-select) each with a keyboard path and a non-drag path, and keyboard shortcuts on list rows, declared in the catalogue rather than coded per widget.
fundamentals.why: docs/design-system.md 'Interaction' declares gestures with keyboard paths (reorder, move, inline-edit, select-many) and ds-lanes exists, so the board is partly covered. Plinth's list rows use letter shortcuts (S, E, U) and Alt+Arrow lane moves that the catalogue does not declare; the gesture set does not include a per-row shortcut. WG-5481 covers gestures, wizards and pending state.

fundamentals.capability: Human-readable sequential numbers per tenant and per kind (task_no, order_no, txn_no), allocated transactionally with no gaps guarantee stated, shown to people and unique within the tenant.
fundamentals.why: Strata record identifiers are opaque ids; no sequence declaration produces a per-tenant counter a product can display. Plinth allocates task_no from suite_counters inside the transaction (contract 2.4). WG-5505 covers identifier sequences.
